security_audit.summary: The static matches are Markdown examples, metadata, or diagnostic addresses, not executable backticks or hidden network calls. The mutable @latest installer remains a medium supply-chain risk; no prompt injection or credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The Go installer references a mutable @latest module version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer to a reviewed module version or immutable commit, then update it through a documented review process.

static_findings.snippet: Use `sonos` to control Sonos speakers on the local network.
- `sonos discover`
- `sonos status --name "Kitchen"`
- `sonos play|pause|stop --name "Kitchen"`
- `sonos volume set 15 --name "Kitchen"`
- Grouping: `sonos group status|join|unjoin|party|solo`
- Favorites: `sonos favorites list|open`
- Queue: `sonos queue list|play|clear`
- Spotify search (via SMAPI): `sonos smapi search --service "Spotify" --category tracks "query"`
- If SSDP fails, specify `--ip <speaker-ip>`.
- Spotify Web API search is optional and requires `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`.

content.user_title: Control Sonos Speakers from Your AI Assistant
content.value_statement: Managing Sonos rooms manually slows routine playback and grouping tasks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused Sonos CLI commands.
actual_capabilities: Discovers Sonos speakers available on the local network.
Retrieves status for a speaker selected by room name.
Controls playback with play, pause, and stop actions.
Sets the volume for a named speaker.
Manages speaker groups, favorites, and playback queues.
Searches Spotify through SMAPI and explains common network permission errors.
limitations: Requires the Sonos CLI binary and network access to the target speakers.
Discovery can fail when SSDP multicast or local network access is blocked.
Optional Spotify Web API search requires separate client credentials.
Available commands and services depend on the installed CLI version and Sonos environment.

use_cases.title: Control Daily Listening
use_cases.description: Discover a room, check its status, and adjust playback or volume with precise commands.

use_cases.title: Manage Multi-Room Audio
use_cases.description: Review groups, join speakers, start party mode, or isolate one room.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Local Discovery
use_cases.description: Match common SSDP and bind errors with local network permission guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Speakers
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover the Sonos speakers on my local network and summarize the rooms you find.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a basic inventory of reachable speakers.

prompt_templates.title: Check and Adjust a Room
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the status of [room name]. Set its volume to [level] only after confirming the selected room.
prompt_templates.scenario: Inspect one room before changing its volume.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Listening Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the current Sonos groups, then join [room A] with [room B]. Report the resulting group.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Sonos discovery error: [error text]. Consider sandbox restrictions, local network permissions, SSDP, and a known speaker IP.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate local networking failures with environment-specific guidance.

output_examples.input: Discover my Sonos speakers and summarize them.
output_examples.output: Three speakers were found: Kitchen, Office, and Living Room. Living Room is the current group coordinator.

output_examples.input: Check Kitchen and set its volume to 15.
output_examples.output: Kitchen is available and currently paused. Its volume was changed from 10 to 15.

output_examples.input: Explain why discovery reports no route to host.
output_examples.output: SSDP multicast cannot reach the local network. Enable local network access for the host process or use an approved network-enabled environment.

best_practices: Use exact room names from discovery before changing playback, volume, or groups.
Confirm disruptive actions, including queue clearing, party mode, and large volume changes.
Use a known speaker IP only when SSDP discovery fails and the address is trusted.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every sandbox permits local network or multicast traffic.
Do not expose Spotify client credentials in prompts, logs, or command output.
Do not clear queues or regroup every room without explicit user scope.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The Sonos CLI binary must be available, and the host must reach your Sonos speakers.

faq.question: Can this skill discover speakers automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Sonos CLI discovery, which depends on SSDP multicast access to the local network.

faq.question: Can it control speaker groups?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents group status, join, unjoin, party, and solo operations.

faq.question: Does Spotify search require credentials?
faq.answer: SMAPI search may use the Sonos service connection. Optional Spotify Web API search requires a client ID and secret.

faq.question: Why does discovery fail in a sandbox?
faq.answer: Some sandboxes block UDP binds, multicast, or local network access. Use approved network permissions or a trusted speaker IP.

faq.question: Does this skill stream audio itself?
faq.answer: No. It controls Sonos devices and services through the installed CLI.
